full_judgment:
37. This appeal arises out of a pre-emption case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. The land under pre-emption represents 2/3rd share of the original permanent tenure recorded in C S. Khatian No 214 of Dhaka city belonging to '"Bangladesh, the remaining 1/3rd share of which belonged to her co sharer Akshoy Kumar. As both the owners held and possessed the tenure in khas the tenure has been referred to as an occupancy raiyati although by a decree in a partition suit- T.S. No. 126 of 1946, they separately possessed their respective shares. Askhoy transferred his 1/3rd share to one Nafisa Khatun by sale deed dated 19 July, 1952, and Nafisa Khatun on her part transferred the same interest to respondent No. 1, who is the pre-emptor in this case, by a sale deed dated 18 April 1972. As to Rangubala's 2/3rd share, she created a lease in favour of Ayesha. Khatun by a registered lease-deed dated 23rd December 1933 and started realizing rent from her at therate of Re. 1/- a year. Ayesha Khatun sold her land to the appellant who is pre-emptee in this case, by a registered sale-deed dated 10 September 1973, and it is this transfer which has given rise to this pre-emption case. 

 "An under-raiyat is upgraded to that of a raiyat when his superior's rent receiving interest came to be acquired by and vested in the government, but such under-raiyat thereby became tenant only with respect to the land held by him as an under-raiyat but this has no connection with regard to the area in khas possession of his erstwhile landlords (i.e. previous raiyats) who became raiyats under the government. In other words, the two portions became two separate entities forming the subject matters of two different tenancies." 

 This decision is not found to have been cited in the case of Anwara Begum, 27 DLR (AD) 109. The principle of law on this subject is that where an under-raiyati is created by a raiyat, the latter is not a co-sharer of the former; and when the superior interest of the raiyat is extinguished and he disappears, the under-raiyat is upgraded into a raiyat but only in respect of his own share. If the previous "raiyat or for that matter his co-sharer raiyat held khas any portion of the original tenancy, that portion becomes a separate raiyati under the government with which the upgraded raiyat bas got no connection. Inview of this position the under-raiyati held by Ayesha upgraded into an independent raiyati which got no connection with the raiyati previously held by Nafisa, now by Respondent No. 1. As such Respondent No. 1 is not a co-sharer of the appellant and he got no right to pre-empt the land purchased by the appellant from Ayesha Khatun. I would, therefore, accept Ground No. 1 of Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed which is alone sufficient to the dispose of this appeal.
